# Two-Page, Parser-Safe CV Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A CV generated by the web app fits two pages at 9.5pt type, keeps the Volunteer section, and reads to a resume parser as one complete record per role.

**Architecture:** Add a `dense` CV template whose every text size derives from one `--font-size` token, with one experience entry per role and no right-aligned gaps. Give the render payload a `volunteer[]` section and fold the competencies grid into Skills when a template has no slot for it. Before the web run saves a tailored CV, it measures the page count of the built HTML and, when that is over the limit, rebuilds the same payload in `dense`. The writer's prompt states the page limit and forbids dropping a `cv.md` section.

**Tech Stack:** Node 24 ESM (`.mjs`), `node:test` and the repo's `pass`/`fail` suites, Playwright Chromium for PDF, the existing `build-cv-html.mjs` and `generate-pdf.mjs` pipeline, Next.js web app under `web/`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/research/2026-11-19-cv-two-page-fit/README.md`. Read it in full first, ending with its Decisions table. Its measurements and its "What parser vendors require" table are the reasons for every decision here.

**Review history:** Rewritten on 2026-11-19 after an independent review against the code found 16 issues, all confirmed. The first draft tested builder functions that are not exported, missed two gates a new payload key must pass, and put the overflow fallback where the route's control flow cannot host it.

## Global Constraints

- Body type in `dense` is `9.5pt`, line height `1.15`, page margin `0.5in`. No text in `dense` is set in `px`.
- `dense` declares its font stack the way `templates/ats/cv-template.ats.html` does: Liberation Sans first, ending `'Arial Unicode MS', sans-serif`. `tests/cv-cjk-pdf-font.test.mjs` enforces that on every template. No `@font-face`, no web font, `font-variant-ligatures: none`.
- No `letter-spacing` and no `text-transform` on any heading in `dense`.
- One experience entry per role. The employer name is never printed once for several roles.
- No element in an experience entry is right-aligned or separated from its neighbors by flex `space-between`.
- The page limit is not raised. `cv.max_pages` keeps its default of 2. Type never shrinks below 9.5pt to make a page count.
- The base template's CSS does not change. `tests/theme-style-tokens.test.mjs` compares a base render byte for byte with `tests/fixtures/theme-style/example-default.html`, and that golden file must still match without being regenerated.
- The repository is public. No personal data: fixtures are synthetic, and the owner's `cv.md`, employer and contact details never enter a file.
- `build-cv-html.mjs` exports nothing. A test drives it by spawning the CLI and reading the JSON report on stdout, as `tests/template-pack-sections.test.mjs:86-94` does.
- Every changed or added path must be named in the "Deviations decided" table of `.claude/skills/upstream-review/SKILL.md`, by full path or by a parent directory with its slash. Add the row in the same commit, then run `node --test tests/fork-deviations-covered.test.mjs` after committing, because that test diffs `HEAD`.
- A new test is its own file under `tests/*.test.mjs` (core) or `web/tests/lib/*.test.mjs` (web). Browser suites declare `toolRequired('browser')`.
- Commits follow Conventional Commits with a scope. Before each commit run `node scripts/check-syntax.mjs` (the real check behind `npm run lint`) and the task's own tests. Work happens in a sibling worktree on branch `feat/cv-dense-template`, never on `main`.
- One PR for the whole plan. Review it once with the four-reviewer pass and local CodeRabbit before the first push.

## Review Focus

- A payload with `volunteer` built with a template that has no `{{VOLUNTEER}}` slot. Expected: a warning that names the template, and in the web run that warning reaches the user. Tests in Task 1 and Task 4.
- A `cv.md` whose Volunteer heading reads "Volunteer Experience", "Volunteering" or "Community Involvement". Expected: all map to the `volunteer` section key, so the section-order check passes. Test in Task 1.
- Volunteer text copied from `cv.md` meeting the fact and voice gates. Expected: it passes, since the source backs it. Test in Task 1.
- A payload with competencies and no `skills` array, built with `dense`. Expected: a Skills section appears holding the folded competencies. Test in Task 2.
- A CV that is over the limit even in `dense`. Expected: the HTML is saved in `dense`, the normal render reports the overflow once, and nothing is built a third time. Test in Task 4.

### Task 2: Fold competencies into Skills when the template has no slot

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/cv-competencies-fold.test.mjs`
- Modify: `build-cv-html.mjs` (`main()` near line 1200 and `runMarkdown()` near line 1109)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `foldCompetencies(payload)` from `ats-payload.mjs:276`. It returns `{ payload, transform }` and never mutates its input. `ats-payload.mjs` imports only `fs` and two `lib/` helpers, so a static import from the builder creates no cycle.
- Produces: in `main()` and `runMarkdown()`, after `validatePayload` and before `templateSlotWarnings`, the payload is replaced by `foldCompetencies(payload).payload` when the template text has no `{{COMPETENCIES}}` token and `payload.competencies` is non-empty. The order matters twice: `templateSlotWarnings` must see the folded payload or it still warns, and `validatePayload` must run first because the fold discards a `skills` value that is not an array.

### Task 3: The `dense` template

**Files:**
- Create: `templates/dense/cv-template.dense.html`, `templates/dense/sections/experience.html`
- Create: `tests/cv-dense-template.test.mjs`
- Modify: `tests/cv-visual/pdf-reading-order.spec.mjs` (one new test), `tests/cv-visual/baselines.json` and `tests/cv-visual/__screenshots__/` (generated)
- Modify: `lib/resume/template-layouts.mjs` (add `dense: ONE_COLUMN`), `templates/README.md` (one row)
- Modify: `.claude/skills/upstream-review/SKILL.md` (a `templates/dense/` row)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the fixture and `{{VOLUNTEER}}` from Task 1, the fold from Task 2.
- Produces: template name `dense`. `resolveTemplate('cv', 'dense')` from `cv-templates.mjs` returns its absolute path as a string.

Start from `templates/ats/cv-template.ats.html`: copy its font-stack declaration, its `--job-break-inside` and `--project-break-inside` defaults and its print rules, which three sweeps over every shipped template require (`tests/cv-cjk-pdf-font.test.mjs`, `tests/theme-style.test.mjs:328`, `tests/template-page-breaks.test.mjs`). The manifest comment is:

```
<!-- career-ops-template
name: Dense
version: 1.0.0
sections: experience
-->
```

`sections: experience` makes a missing or malformed partial an error. Without it the builder falls back to its built-in entry, which puts the company and the date side by side.

Template rules, each from the spec:

- `:root` sets `--font-size: 9.5pt`, `--line-height: 1.15`, `--page-margin: 0.5in`, `--section-gap: 6pt`, `--item-gap: 7pt`, so the profile `style:` block overrides them. Every other size is in `em`: name `1.9em`, title line `1.1em`, section headings `1.1em` bold, dates and locations `1em`.
- Slots, in this order: header (name, title, contact row), `{{SUMMARY_TEXT}}`, `{{EXPERIENCE}}`, `{{PROJECTS}}`, `{{EDUCATION}}`, `{{CERTIFICATIONS}}`, `{{AWARDS}}`, `{{SKILLS}}`, `{{VOLUNTEER}}`, consent. No `{{COMPETENCIES}}` slot, so Task 2 folds it. Section comments match `SECTION_MARKER_RE` (`<!-- WORK EXPERIENCE -->`).
- `.skills-grid` is `display: block` with one row per category, so two categories never share a line.
- The experience partial, exactly:

```html
<!--ENTRY-->
<div class="job">
  <div class="job-role">{{ROLE}}</div>
  <div class="job-meta"><span class="job-company">{{COMPANY}}</span>{{LOCATION_BLOCK}} | <span class="job-period">{{PERIOD}}</span></div>
  {{CONTEXT_BLOCK}}
  <ul>
    {{BULLETS}}
  </ul>
</div>
<!--LOCATION_BLOCK-->, <span class="job-location">{{LOCATION}}</span><!--/LOCATION_BLOCK-->
<!--CONTEXT_BLOCK--><div class="job-context">{{CONTEXT}}</div><!--/CONTEXT_BLOCK-->
<!--/ENTRY-->
```

`.job-meta` and its spans are inline text. The separators are literal characters in the markup, never CSS `content`.

### Task 4: Choose `dense` before saving when the built CV is over the limit

The first draft of this plan re-rendered after a failed PDF render. The route cannot host that: its `renderPdf` (`web/src/app/api/run/route.ts:708-736`) sends the final event and closes the stream itself, `renderAndMarkPdf` returns no stderr and no draft path, and each render attempt deletes the saved HTML. So the choice is made earlier, inside `materializeTailoredCv`, which already builds in a scratch directory and returns warnings. The route does not change.

**Files:**
- Create: `web/src/lib/core/page-budget.mjs`, `web/src/lib/cv-fit.mjs`, `web/tests/lib/cv-fit.test.mjs`
- Modify: `web/src/lib/cv-from-json.mjs` (`materializeTailoredCv`, lines 216 to 256)
- Modify: `web/tests/lib/cv-from-json.test.mjs`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces, in `web/src/lib/core/page-budget.mjs`, following the pattern of `web/src/lib/core/page-format.mjs`:

```js
/** @returns {Promise<{ maxPages: number }>} 2 when cv.max_pages is unset or unusable. */
export async function readPageBudget(coreRoot, dataRoot)
```

It calls the core's `readCvPageBudget` from `theme-style.mjs:206` and never parses the profile itself.

- Produces, in `web/src/lib/cv-fit.mjs`:

```js
/** Pages of a built CV, from an isolated render that indexes nothing. null when it cannot be measured. */
export async function countCvPages({ html, format, coreRoot, profilePath, spawnFn, execPath }): Promise<number | null>

/** @returns {Promise<{ template: string, html: string, fallback: null | { from: string, pages: number } }>} */
export async function chooseFittingTemplate({ template, denseTemplate, maxPages, build, countPages })
```

`countCvPages` writes the HTML into a fresh temp directory, runs `generate-pdf.mjs <html> <pdf> --format=<format> --max-pages=99 --skip-fact-check` with `CAREER_OPS_ROOT` set to that directory and `CAREER_OPS_PROFILE` to the real profile, exactly as `renderMasterPdf` in `web/src/lib/cv-master-pdf.mjs:60-63` isolates its render, reads the count from the `📊 Pages: N` line, and removes the directory. `chooseFittingTemplate` calls `build(template)`, which returns the built HTML, then `countPages(html)`. When the count is over `maxPages` and `template !== denseTemplate`, it calls `build(denseTemplate)` once and returns that with `fallback` set. A `null` count means "do not fall back".

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `web/tests/lib/cv-fit.test.mjs`, with stub `build` and `countPages` functions that record their calls.

## Not in this plan

- Tagged PDF output (`tagged: true` on `page.pdf()`). It works (tested) and no source says a parser reads it.
- DOCX for upload. Both parser vendors prefer Word and `lib/resume/export/docx.mjs` exists, but its layout is unmeasured. Worth its own research once the parser check has a baseline.
- A Volunteer slot in the six templates other than base, `ats` and `dense`. They warn instead of dropping. Add a slot when someone uses one.
- A Volunteer section in LaTeX output. `UNRENDERED_SECTIONS.tex` says so plainly.
- Keeping the payload on disk to re-run the fact gate without a new agent run. Task 4 does not need it.
- A size ladder below 9.5pt. The fallback stops at `dense`.
